key_insight: SQD remains chemically accurate even when the sampling circuit is heavily compressed, because it only needs bitstrings with enough ground-state overlap rather than a precise variational solution.
engineering_relevance: This enables much shallower, faster quantum chemistry circuits by pruning low-impact gates and rounding angles to Clifford values, reducing resource demands on both simulators and hardware.
method: Gradient-based operator pruning removes low-impact excitation operators from the VQE ansatz.
Clifford rounding snaps remaining parameters to the nearest Clifford angle to simplify the circuit.
Both compression methods are applied before SQD-based classical post-processing on a qubit-reduced Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: Across 21 molecules, median SQD error stayed within chemical accuracy at 50% compression on both axes, with up to 33× simulation speedup and hardware validation on 6 molecules showing up to 2.8× depth reduction without loss in SQD accuracy.
watch_item: Compression is robust in the reported tests, but it still depends on maintaining sufficient ground-state overlap, so aggressive pruning or rounding may fail for harder molecules or different ansätze.
paper_title: SQD-Enabled Circuit Compression for Resource-Efficient Quantum Chemistry
